title: Roy Eldridge's band at the Three Deuces, with Zutty featured
summary: After Fletcher Henderson's Grand Terrace troubles and the flooding of the Three Deuces floor, Roy Eldridge's band came in with Joe Eldridge, Truck Parham, Teddy Cole and Johnny Collins while Zutty remained the feature.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs

blocks.x: Well, Roy used to come in and sit in with us see. Because he was with Fletcher Henderson at the Grande Terrace at the time. So, Fletcher and the Grande Terrace had some kind of trouble and Roy quit you know. And then Roy after Sam, opened up the Three Dances again because the river had broke in and had flooded the dance floor. Yes, because it was in the basement you know, so when Sam opened again he had Roy Eldridge to come in you see with his band.
But I was still the feature you know.
And that was the band in which Roy had his brother?
That's right, yes. His brother, Scoop's Carey and Dave Young. And Truck Parham and Bumble Bee Slim, I used to call him, Johnny Collins on guitar.
(LAUGHTER?) What did you call him Bumble Bee Slim for?
Well because he reminded me of Bumble Bee Slim. I'd give guys names you know and they would stick. (LAUGHTER). Bumble Bee Slim. And we had Teddy Cole on piano. That was Cozy's brother you know.
Oh Cozy's brother?
Yes, Cozy's brother.
Eddie Cole or Teddy Cole?
No, Teddy Cole.
Teddy Cole. There was an Eddie Cole wasn't there?
Eddie Cole, he...
He's still around.
He used to be with Nobie la Sisslo (Gioserole?) a long time.
Well was he any relation of Nat Cole?
Yes, why sure.
Eddie Cole was his brother?
Why sure, that's right.
Well that was a good little band.
Oh it was. It was a real lovely, lovely band. And Joe was making all the arrangements for us you know.
